extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (or advanced undergraduates) studying algebraic geometry / homological algebra (readers of Math 216 / Ravi Vakil's The Rising Sea)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, computation methods, and key theorems about derived functors (L_i, R^i), Ext and Tor, δ-functors, Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions, the Grothendieck and Leray spectral sequences, and the agreement of Čech and derived functor cohomology for quasicoherent sheaves on quasicompact separated schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation for derived functors
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a right-exact functor, its left-derived functors are denoted L_iF (with L_0F = F). If F is left-exact, its right-derived functors are denoted R^iF (the superscript indicates that the long exact sequence is 'ascending in i').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use superscript notation for right-derived functors and subscript for left-derived; record L_0F = F and R^0F = F as appropriate so that long exact sequences align with index orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two equivalent definitions of Ext
rubrics_metrics.description: Ext^i_A(M,N) may be defined either (D) by taking a projective resolution of M and viewing Ext^i as the ith right-derived functor of Hom(·,N) applied to M, or (E) by taking an injective resolution of N and viewing Ext^i as the ith right-derived functor of Hom(M,·) applied to N; these two definitions agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State and use the corresponding long exact sequences for Ext; verify equivalence (see Exercise 23.3.B). Choose the viewpoint convenient for the computation (projective vs injective resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness of Ext over Noetherian rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and M and N are finitely generated A-modules, then Ext^i_A(M,N) is a finitely generated A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove using the projective-resolution definition of Ext (Exercise 23.2.F). Use this when checking finiteness properties in algebraic geometry contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category ModA has enough injectives
rubrics_metrics.description: For any ring A, the category Mod_A of A-modules has enough injectives (i.e., every module admits a monomorphism into an injective module).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof is sketched via embedding modules into injective Z-modules and then into Hom_Z(A, Q) (Exercises 23.2.I–K). Use axiom of choice / Zorn's lemma where indicated for constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of injective Z-modules
rubrics_metrics.description: A Z-module (abelian group) Q is injective iff it is divisible (for every nonzero n in Z and q in Q there exists q' with n q' = q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to show quotients of injective Z-modules are injective and to build injective embeddings of arbitrary Z-modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom_Z(A,Q) is injective as an A-module
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is an injective Z-module and A is a ring, then Hom_Z(A,Q) (with the natural A-module structure) is an injective A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction is used in the proof that Mod_A has enough injectives (Exercise 23.2.J). Carefully define the A-action on Hom_Z(A,Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a (cohomological) δ-functor
rubrics_metrics.description: A δ-functor from an abelian category A to another abelian category B is a collection of additive functors T^i: A → B (T^i = 0 for i<0) together with connecting morphisms δ^i: T^i(A'') → T^{i+1}(A') for each short exact sequence 0 → A' → A → A'' → 0, satisfying (i) the induced long sequence is exact (so T^0 is left-exact) and (ii) functoriality: morphisms of short exact sequences yield commutative diagrams of the δ^i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing or checking a δ-functor, verify both the long exactness property and naturality/functoriality of the δ-maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality of δ-functors
rubrics_metrics.description: A δ-functor (T^i, δ^i) is universal if for any other δ-functor (T'^i, δ'^i) and any natural transformation α: T^0 → T'^0 there is a unique morphism of δ-functors extending α. If a left-exact functor F is given, there is at most one universal δ-functor extending it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use universality to identify derived functors as the unique (when exists) universal δ-functor extending T^0 = F; employ Exercise 23.2.L for morphisms of δ-functors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient condition for universality (Theorem 23.2.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (T^i, δ^i) is a covariant δ-functor and for every object A there exists a monomorphism A → J with T^i(J) = 0 for all i>0, then (T^i, δ^i) is universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a route to prove universality using 'enough' objects annihilating higher T^i; the hypothesis can be weakened to effaceability (Remark 23.2.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effaceable functor notion
rubrics_metrics.description: An additive functor F: A → B is effaceable if for every object A there exists a monomorphism A → J with F(J)=0. The hypothesis of Theorem 23.2.8 can be weakened to require only that T^i be effaceable for each i>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effaceability is the more general (and often used) condition in classical references (Weibel, Lang, Grothendieck).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry of Tor
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an isomorphism Tor^A_i(M,N) ≅ Tor^A_i(N,M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by taking free (or flat) resolutions of both arguments, forming a double complex (product), and comparing the two spectral sequences arising from the two filtrations (Exercise 23.3.A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derived functors via acyclic resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: If F: A→B is right-exact and A has enough projectives, an object A∈A is F-acyclic if L_iF(A)=0 for i>0. Derived functors of F can be computed by taking resolutions by F-acyclic objects (e.g., flat resolutions to compute Tor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct resolutions by F-acyclic objects, truncate, apply F, and take homology (Exercise 23.3.C). Use the projective-resolution-of-a-complex trick (Hint 23.3.3) when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck composition-of-functors spectral sequence (Theorem 23.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose F: A→B and G: B→C are left-exact additive covariant functors, and A and B have enough injectives. If F sends injective objects of A to G-acyclic objects of B, then for each X∈A there is a spectral sequence with E2_{p,q} = R^qG(R^pF(X)) converging to R^{p+q}(G∘F)(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spectral sequence is the general formalism behind Leray; hypotheses about acyclicity of F on injectives are essential. The E2 page is independent of choices; the proof uses injective resolutions, Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions, and double-complex spectral-sequence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and use of Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a complex C• in an abelian category, one can build a double complex I_{p,q} (a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution) whose rows and columns are exact and whose associated Z_p, B_p, and H_p complexes are injective resolutions of the corresponding objects; this facilitates two spectral-sequence filtrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct injective resolutions of cycles, boundaries, and homology and arrange them in the double complex (Exercises 23.3.E–G). Use the resolution to compare different orientations of the spectral sequence in proofs such as Theorem 23.3.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of sheaf cohomology via derived functors
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ringed space (X, O_X) and O_X-module F, define H^i(X,F) := R^i Γ(X, F). For a morphism π: (X,O_X)→(Y,O_Y), derived pushforwards R^iπ_*: Mod_{O_X}→Mod_{O_Y} are defined similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This derived-functor definition extends older Čech constructions and is used for general sheaf cohomology and higher direct images; compare with earlier special-case definitions (Chapter 18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Category of O_X-modules has enough injectives (Theorem 23.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any ringed space (X,O_X), the category Mod_{O_X} of O_X-modules has enough injectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct injective skyscraper sheaves at stalks and take their product over X (Exercises 23.4.A–C). Use this to justify existence of derived functors for sheaves on general ringed spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flasque (flabby) sheaf definition and basic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf F on a topological space is flasque if all restriction maps res_{U⊂V}: F(V) → F(U) are surjective for all opens U⊂V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flasqueness to deduce: (a) if 0→F'→F→F''→0 and F' is flasque then the sequence of sections over any U is exact; (b) pushforwards of flasque sheaves are flasque; (c) injective sheaves are flasque (Exercise 23.4.D–F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flasque implies Γ-acyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is a flasque O_X-module then H^i(X,F) = 0 for i>0 (i.e., F is Γ-acyclic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by embedding F into an injective, using that injectives are flasque and chasing the long exact sequence in cohomology (Exercise 23.4.G). This is used to show pushforwards of injectives are acyclic for Γ and hence to derive Leray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leray spectral sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π: (X,O_X)→(Y,O_Y) of ringed spaces and any O_X-module F, there is a spectral sequence with E2-term H^q(Y, R^pπ_* F) abutting to H^{p+q}(X,F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows from the Grothendieck spectral sequence by checking that π_* sends injectives to Γ-acyclic objects (use injective⇒flasque⇒pushforward flasque⇒Γ-acyclic).

rubrics_metrics.name: Čech cohomology equals derived functor cohomology (Theorem 23.5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasicompact separated scheme and F is a quasicoherent sheaf, then Čech cohomology of F (with respect to finite affine covers, properly defined) agrees with the derived functor cohomology H^i(X,F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof uses a double complex built from an injective resolution and a finite affine open cover and compares the two filtrations (spectral-sequence argument). One needs two vanishing ingredients: (A) injective sheaves have no Čech cohomology for finite covers, and (B) on affines, R^iΓ(X, F) = 0 for i>0 when F is quasicoherent. The isomorphism is functorial and compatible with long exact sequences (Exercises 23.5.G–H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredient (A) for Čech vs derived: injectives have no Čech cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is an injective O_X-module and X = ⋃ U_i is a finite open cover, then Q has no i-th Čech cohomology with respect to this cover for i>0 (equivalently, flasque sheaves have trivial higher Čech cohomology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by induction on the number of opens using exact sequences of Čech complexes and the flasque property (Exercise 23.5.C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ingredient (B) for Čech vs derived: affines are Γ-acyclic for quasicoherent sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an affine scheme and F is a quasicoherent sheaf on X, then R^iΓ(X,F) = 0 for all i>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by induction using a tailored affine cover of X adapted to a cohomology class and the double-complex spectral-sequence argument (section 23.5.4). Quasicoherence is essential in the argument to ensure vanishing of the relevant Čech terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working in QCoh_X vs Mod_{O_X}
rubrics_metrics.description: One can work in the category QCoh_X of quasicoherent sheaves rather than Mod_{O_X}, but QCoh_X lacks some convenient exact functors (like extension by zero), making some arguments harder; QCoh_X has enough injectives if X is Noetherian, and in many cases derived functors computed in QCoh_X agree with those in Mod_{O_X}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For simplicity and availability of adjoints (i_!, extension by zero) the text works in Mod_{O_X}; when needed, use additional results (Mur, EE) to transfer statements to QCoh_X and to relax separatedness hypotheses to quasiseparated in the Noetherian case (23.5.7–8).
